newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters urge China to release dissident Wang.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters urge China to release dissident Wang.

text.p: Pro-democracy activists took to the streets in Hong Kong on Friday evening to protest against China's rejection of the appeal of dissident Wang Dan who has been sentenced to 11 years in jail for subversion.

"Release Wan Dan. Release all dissidents," about 50 demonstrators chanted as they marched through a busy commercial district to the local branch of the Xinhua news agency, China's de facto diplomatic mission in the territory.
On Friday, China rejected the 27-year-old dissident's appeal and upheld his 11-year prison sentence for subversion handed down last month.
The former student leader had already served four years in prison for his role in the 1989 Beijing democracy demonstrations that were crushed by the Chinese army.

The jailing of Wang was the latest in a series of crushing blows to China's struggling democracy movement. Most dissidents have already been forced into exile or are serving long sentences in prison or labour camps.
Wang's plight escalated fears over future freedoms in Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight next June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Earlier on Friday, a group of demonstrators urging Wang's release picketed a historic meeting of an electoral committee charged with selecting the territory's first post-colonial leader.
